cross_component: Canonical digest identity must agree across cache, exception matching, permit binding, and audit.
Immutable policy snapshot must agree across source/digest gates, scanner cache validation, exception evaluation, and permit issuance.
Decision completion is contingent on durable audit commit, not merely in-memory evaluation.
Recovery rebuilds derived state from durable history without changing security evidence semantics.
edge_boundary: Cache entry at TTL boundary versus just beyond TTL.
Exception and permit exactly at expiry boundary.
Same artifact name or mutable tag resolving to a new digest.
Policy version and scanner DB revision changes with existing cache state.
Restart after durable audit append but before derived projection update.
failure_recovery: Scanner outage with and without a current valid cache entry.
Crash after journal write and before projection write.
Malformed journal tail while preserving earlier valid history.
Partially written cache record on startup.
negative_rejection: Scanner unavailable or stale scanner DB evidence.
Critical/high vulnerability without exact current exception.
Exception with wrong digest, surface, environment, policy code, or expiry.
Permit tamper, wrong instance, wrong digest, wrong policy version, or expiry.
normal: Clean package/container/dependency acquisitions with trusted source and immutable digest follow one policy pipeline.
Fresh scanner evidence permits clean artifacts and produces exact-scope permits.
Current exact-scope vulnerability exceptions permit only the intended vulnerable artifact.
Valid digest-scoped cache evidence survives normal restart without unnecessary rescanning.
Every allow and deny is reflected in the durable journal and last-decision projection.

defects.observable_failure: A direct dpkg acquisition bypasses the package trusted-source gate that apt requests use.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing only apt routing leaves lower-level package managers outside the canonical policy path.

defects.observable_failure: A Maven dependency request is classified outside the dependency surface and skips dependency source policy.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding a Maven-specific allowlist duplicates policy semantics and still permits divergence across managers.

defects.observable_failure: A mutable container tag is treated as the cache identity after the registry resolves it to a different digest.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Clearing cache on one tag update hides the symptom but does not make digest the canonical artifact identity.

defects.observable_failure: A required-digest policy accepts a request whose digest field is empty when the manager supplies a version or tag.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking digest only in selected adapters leaves another acquisition surface able to bypass the invariant.

defects.observable_failure: A scanner outage is interpreted as no vulnerabilities and produces an allow decision without current evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Returning an empty vulnerability list on scanner error still fails open even if later severity logic is correct.

defects.observable_failure: A cached clean result is reused after the scanner database revision changes.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding TTL validation alone still accepts evidence created under an obsolete scanner database.

defects.observable_failure: A cached result created under an older policy version is reused after vulnerability policy changes.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Keying by digest and scanner DB but not policy version preserves stale decision semantics.

defects.observable_failure: An expired cache entry is accepted because freshness is checked from file modification time instead of the recorded evidence timestamp and TTL.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Touching or rewriting cache files can make stale evidence look fresh unless expiry is part of the stored contract.

defects.observable_failure: An expired vulnerability exception continues to suppress a deny decision.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing expiry alone still leaves overbroad scope and ordering errors.

defects.observable_failure: An exception for one artifact digest is applied to another digest sharing the same package name or coordinate.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Matching name/version plus expiry still violates immutable artifact scoping.

defects.observable_failure: A dependency-surface exception is applied to a container acquisition with the same digest.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Digest-only exception matching remains cross-surface and overbroad.

defects.observable_failure: A vulnerability exception is evaluated before trusted-source and scanner-evidence gates and therefore overrides a non-exemptable denial.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Making the exception matcher narrower does not repair policy ordering if it can still bypass source/evidence prerequisites.

defects.observable_failure: A permit signature can be reproduced using an unkeyed checksum of visible permit fields.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Switching hash algorithms without a secret still permits off-host forgery.

defects.observable_failure: A valid permit remains accepted after its instance_id is changed to another EC2 instance.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Signing only artifact fields leaves instance binding forgeable or replayable.

defects.observable_failure: A permit issued for one artifact digest validates for another digest under the same request identifier.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Binding request ID without digest does not bind the security decision to immutable artifact identity.

defects.observable_failure: An expired permit verifies successfully because expiry is not enforced against the decision clock.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Authenticating all fields but skipping time validity preserves replay after authorization should end.

defects.observable_failure: Deny decisions are returned to the caller but never appended to the durable audit journal.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Logging only successful decisions leaves exactly the security-relevant deny history missing.

defects.observable_failure: The command reports completion before audit.jsonl is fsynced, allowing a crash to lose a reported decision.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Flushing buffered I/O without fsync can still acknowledge a decision that is not durable.

defects.observable_failure: last-decision.json is updated before the corresponding audit append, exposing a latest decision absent from durable history.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Making the projection atomic is insufficient if commit ordering still lets it lead the journal.

defects.observable_failure: Restart repair truncates or recreates audit.jsonl when it encounters a malformed tail, deleting previously valid history.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deleting the journal restores parseability by violating the history-preservation invariant.

defects.observable_failure: Startup accepts a partially written scan-cache record and uses it as valid security evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Ignoring parse errors or defaulting missing fields can silently convert corruption into permissive evidence.

defects.observable_failure: Two concurrent evaluations overwrite shared last-decision state so its contents do not correspond to the final durable audit append.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding a mutex only around the projection leaves journal/projection ordering inconsistent unless the whole commit boundary is serialized.

defects.observable_failure: One evaluation observes a policy version that differs from the version used to validate its cache entry and issue its permit.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Locking individual components cannot provide a coherent decision if policy/evidence/permit do not share one immutable snapshot.

defects.observable_failure: A restart between audit append and projection update treats the durable decision as incomplete and appends a duplicate decision record on recovery.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Replaying every last journal record blindly can duplicate committed history rather than rebuilding only derived state.

RC1_CANONICAL_IDENTITY.invariant: Every manager-specific request must normalize to one surface/source/digest identity before policy evaluation.

RC2_EVIDENCE_CACHE_FRESHNESS.invariant: Scanner/cache evidence is usable only for the exact digest, policy version, scanner DB revision, and valid TTL.

RC3_EXCEPTION_SCOPE_ORDERING.invariant: Exceptions are evaluated only after source/digest/evidence gates and match exact allowed scope while unexpired.

RC4_PERMIT_AUTHENTICITY_SCOPE.invariant: ALLOW permits are keyed, time-bounded, and bound to the exact request, instance, digest, and policy version.

RC5_DURABLE_DECISION_HISTORY.invariant: Every decision is durably appended and fsynced before completion; last-decision is only a projection.

RC6_RECOVERY_CONCURRENCY.invariant: Recovery and concurrent evaluations cannot expose partial state, regress durable history, or reuse inconsistent snapshots.
